paragraphs.text: Project-scoped skill roots for DeepSeek Harness: the skill symlink you miss from Hermes, with multi-
level category discovery
[](https://github.com/MYSTERY2019/dsh-skills-symlink/releases) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/dee
pseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
English · 中文
Give every project in DeepSeek Harness (DSH) its own set of skills. It replaces the skill symlink fr
om Hermes: one shared library, and each project loads only the categories it lists. The plugin creat
es no symbolic links; the name only borrows the Hermes term.
## ✨ Highlights
- 🗂️ **Per-project skill sets**: one `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` per project, and each project sees only

what it lists
- 📚 **One path for a categorised library**: `maxDepth` reads `category/skill/SKILL.md

` layouts up to 6 levels deep
- 🔥 **Hot reload**: add or remove a skill without restarting DSH
- 🛡️
**Safe by default**: paths and symlinks outside the project are rejected, and the plugin makes no ou

tbound requests
- 🩺 **Diagnostics built in**: a log of every root scanned, plus a post-install check

script
- 🧭 **Visual overview**: see each project's skill mix on the Plugins page
## 🤔 Why
If you came from Hermes, you will miss its skill symlink. A skill lives once in a central repository
, and any project that wants it symlinks it into its own skills directory. Edit the original and eve
ry project follows, with nothing to copy. Project A links the three writing skills, project B links
the two tools skills, and each sees exactly its own set. Adding a skill is one more link; nothing el
ls skills, and each sees exactly its own set. Adding a skill is one more link; nothing else changes.
DSH replaced that with skill roots configured through `customSkillDirs`. Three things break on the w
aced that with skill roots configured through `customSkillDirs`. Three things break on the way over.
First, each root only accepts `<root>/<skill>/SKILL.md`. A library laid out as `category/skill/SKILL
.md` yields nothing when you point at the parent, with no error and no log line.
Second, the setting belongs to the host or the preset, not to the project. Every project sees the sa
me skills, and "this project sees category A only" cannot be expressed.
Third, every skill's name and description goes into context each turn. With a large library that cos
t is fixed and cannot be scoped down.
This plugin moves the paths into the project, one `.dsh/skill-paths.yaml` per project, and `maxDepth
` in the plugin row lets it read category folders, so a single parent path is enough. From one libra
ry, project A loads 17 skills and project B loads 28.
One library, two projects: A loads 17 skills, B loads 28.

A shared library outside the project needs `allowExternalPaths` in the plugin row first (see Configu
ration). Without it, that entry is skipped and the log says why:

The project file knows two keys, `version` and `skillPaths`. Options such as `maxDepth` and `ignore`
belong to the plugin row; written into the project file they have no effect. The plugin ignores the
m, logs where they belong, and still loads the paths. An invalid entry (outside the project, not a s

### One path for a categorised library
If the library is laid out as `category/skill/SKILL.md`, the project file still names the parent:

## 🔒 Security
The plugin reads files only while DSH resolves skills, and writes only the selected workspace's `.ds
h/skill-paths.yaml` when you save the settings card. It makes no outbound requests and reads no cred
paths.yaml` when you save the settings card. It makes no outbound requests and reads no credentials.
- Absolute paths and `..` are rejected by default. Whether a path is inside the project is decided b
y its real path, so a symbolic link inside the project that points outside is rejected too, and chec
ked again when a skill's body is loaded. Cloning someone else's repository cannot make DSH read othe

r files on your machine.
- Writes go only to workspaces DSH knows, are refused when the `.dsh` folde
r or the config file is a symbolic link, and go through a temporary file and a rename, so a half-wri

tten file is never left behind.
- A write request must be same-origin, `application/json`, and at mo

is never left behind.
- A write request must be same-origin, `application/json`, and at most 16 KB.
